You are a TLA+ specification engineer. You will receive a natural language description of a system. Produce a complete, syntactically correct TLA+ specification that faithfully captures the described behavior. The output must be a valid TLA+ module that passes the SANY parser. Include the MODULE declaration, EXTENDS, CONSTANTS, VARIABLES, Init, Next and Spec. Include all safety invariants and liveness properties described, and any fairness conditions mentioned. Output only the TLA+ specification.

System description: This is a test or validation module rather than a real system model. It checks the correctness of TLA+'s subset-equality (`\subseteq`) operator as applied to power sets (`SUBSET`) of various integer ranges and finite sets.

The single variable `b` is initialized to `TRUE` and updated by `Next` to the conjunction of ten specific subset-equality assertions involving power sets. These assertions verify expected relationships such as: `SUBSET (1..23)` is contained in `SUBSET (1..42)` but not vice versa; `SUBSET (2..42)` is contained in `SUBSET (1..42)` but not vice versa; `SUBSET {1,2,3}` is contained in `SUBSET {1,2,3,4}`; the power set of the empty set is contained in itself and in `SUBSET {1}`; and `SUBSET {1}` is contained in both `SUBSET Int` and `SUBSET Nat`. The invariant `Inv` asserts that `b` remains `TRUE` and is a `BOOLEAN`, meaning all ten subset-equality assertions must hold simultaneously. If the TLA+ evaluator computes any of these relationships incorrectly, `b` would become `FALSE` and the invariant would be violated. The specification thus serves as a model-checking regression test for the semantics of `\subseteq` over power sets of integer-based domains.
